title: GLU Gate Lab
summary: An interactive lab for the 22 feed-forward gates of my stairs study: their shapes, their slopes, and a live layer of hidden units.
excerpt: An interactive lab for the 22 feed-forward gates of my stairs study. On loss nothing beat SwiGLU; the exact Game of Life rule on top of it tied. See each gate's shape, its slope, and a live layer of hidden units.

title: Model whisperers

image.alt: whisperers. The gibberish turned out to be the interesting part. Plate V, a whisper coming apart into tokens, printed in cyanotype.

summary: Gibberish token prefixes, found by optimizing against a model's internals, that make it perform functions no human reading them would guess.
excerpt: A whisperer is a discrete prefix found by optimizing an internal model state or mechanism, rather than giving a direct, explicit instruction toward a desired behavior. Searched against function vectors and filter heads, these prefixes make OLMo perform functions no human reading them would guess.

title: I built a public arena where people attack a "pro-human" steering direction
epistemicStatus: Small empirical writeup, $0 budget, all results public. Two hypotheses failed. Human behavior evaluation still pending.
summary: I extracted a "pro-human values" direction from OLMo-3-32B and built a public leaderboard where people try to move the model along or against it.
excerpt: I extracted a "pro-human values" direction from OLMo-3-32B and built a public leaderboard where people try to move the model along or against it. Token-soup beats "be kind and honest." Anti-human pushes transfer across models 80% of the time; pro-human pushes transfer 33% and have negative rank correlation with Llama-70B. Both my explanations for why failed.

title: The Scout-Refiner Bottleneck: A Negative Result with a Surprising Twist
epistemicStatus: Negative results from a small-scale (~125M param) experiment. The architecture is genuinely novel; none of that helped.
summary: I designed a two-stage attention module with a width bottleneck, expecting it to be more parameter-efficient than standard MHA.
excerpt: I designed a two-stage attention module with a width bottleneck, expecting it to be more parameter-efficient than standard MHA. At equal token budget, the baseline beats every variant by 0.19–0.31 nats. But there's a crossover: at short training budgets, one variant actually wins.
